content:
The parabola can be written in vertex form  

\[
2y=x^{2}-8x+12\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 
y=\frac{x^{2}-8x+12}{2}= \frac{(x-4)^2}{2}-2 .
\]

Hence its vertex is \((4,-2)\) and its slope is  

\[
y' = x-4 .
\]

A circle with centre \((4,39)\) and radius \(r\) has equation  

\[
(x-4)^2+(y-39)^2=r^{2}.
\]

At a point \((x,y)\) of intersection the slopes of the two curves must be equal.
The slope of the circle at \((x,y)\) (the tangent line is perpendicular to the
radius) is  

\[
m_{\text{circle}}=-\frac{x-4}{\,y-39\,}.
\]

Equating the two slopes gives  

\[
x-4 = -\frac{x-4}{y-39}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(x-4)\bigl[(y-39)+1\bigr]=0 .
\]

Thus a tangency can occur only in one of the two cases  

\[
\boxed{x=4}\qquad\text{or}\qquad\boxed{y=38}.
\]

---

### 1.  Case \(x=4\)

The parabola gives \(y=-2\).  
The point \((4,-2)\) lies on the circle, so  

\[
r = \sqrt{(4-4)^2+(-2-39)^2}=|39-(-2)|=41 .
\]

Both the parabola (horizontal tangent) and the circle (tangent perpendicular
to the vertical radius) have a horizontal tangent, so the curves are tangent
at this point.

---

### 2.  Case \(y=38\)

Insert \(y=38\) into the parabola:

\[
38 = \frac{(x-4)^2}{2}-2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad (x-4)^2 = 80 .
\]

Hence  

\[
x-4 = \pm\sqrt{80}= \pm 4\sqrt5,\qquad 
x = 4\pm 4\sqrt5 .
\]

For either point the radius is

\[
r = \sqrt{(x-4)^2+(38-39)^2}
     = \sqrt{80+1}= \sqrt{81}=9 .
\]

At these two points the circle meets the parabola with equal slopes, i.e. the
curves are tangent there.

---

No other tangencies are possible, because the slope‑equality condition
covers all possibilities.

Therefore the real radii for which the circle is tangent to the parabola are  

\[
r=9 \quad\text{and}\quad r=41 .
\]

The required sum is  

\[
9+41 = 50 .
\]

\[
\boxed{50}
\]
